correctness.rationale: For every \(K_{1,a,b}\) a,b>=1, triangle forbids a monochromatic vertex set on all N vertices, so each color forest has at most N-s_c-1 edges. Summation gives the sharp integer lower bound. Explicit hub-star assignments attain the values for a=1,2 and a=3,b>=6. The \(K_{1,3,5}\) four-color certificate, directly checked with verify.py, proves the remaining a=3,b<=5 cases by vertex deletion. Equality M=4(N-1)-N=23 forces each color-edge forest to be a spanning tree on the available complement. Standard-library checks succeeded on 597 instances/182077 graph edges.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-family determination for \(K_{1,a,b}\) with min(a,b)<=3 in the recently studied forest–forest total coloring model, including a sharp exceptional delayed threshold at \(K_{1,3,5}\); exhibits a 23-edge four-color decomposition that beats the natural 5-color hub-star-plus-bipartite-arboricity scheme. Equality makes the edge colors complementary spanning trees in every optimal witness, providing structural rigidity beyond a parameter count.
